Full Statement: Grades PK – 5

Standard 1: The physically literate individual will demonstrate competency in a variety of motor skills and movement patterns.

Rationale: Students in early elementary will observe, learn, practice, and develop basic (fundamental) locomotor (traveling actions), non-locomotor (movement in place), and manipulative (object handling) movements. This foundation continues to be established and reinforced to facilitate motor skill acquisition which give students the capacity for successful levels of performance as they mature. By the end of 5th grade, students continue to achieve maturity with locomotor (traveling actions), non-locomotor (movement in place) and manipulative (object handling) skills. They begin the process of integrating (putting together) these skills into a variety of individual and small sided team sports and activities that have been adapted to their developmental level.

Standard 2: The physically literate individual applies knowledge of concepts, principles, strategies and tactics related to movement and performance.

Rationale: Students in early elementary learn to utilize cognitive information to understand motor skill acquisition. Knowledge of basic movement concepts (body, spatial, directional, and temporal awareness) enhance independent learning and effective participation in physical activity. As they gain more motor control, students begin to adapt their skills in order to produce efficient movement to improve their individual performances. By the end of 5th grade students demonstrate an understanding of movement concepts (body awareness, spatial awareness, qualities of movement, relationships) and mature (proficient) movement forms. They self-assess their skills and those of classmates and discuss methods for improving performance.

Standard 3: The physically literate individual demonstrates the knowledge and skills to achieve and maintain a health-enhancing level of physical activity and fitness.

Rationale: Students in early elementary will learn regular participation in physical activity enhances physical and psychological health, provides for social opportunities, and contributes to a healthy active lifestyle. By the end of 5th grade students develop a more thorough understanding of the relationship between lifestyle and health. Through observation and analysis, students are able to critique self and others as they begin to develop an awareness of the physical, mental, social, and emotional importance of physical activity. Students are able to describe how improved fitness is achieved and identify what their age appropriate physical fitness goals should be.

Rationale: Students in early elementary will develop respect for individual similarities and differences through positive interaction in physical activity. Students will understand that cooperation and teamwork promote personal and group success in activity settings. By the end of 5th grade students begin to show competence for working independently and cooperatively, in pairs and small groups, as they observe, explore, and apply the principles of physical activity in both physical education class and after school. They are willing to work with classmates of varying abilities and interests and are able to apply conflict management skills when needed.

Rationale: Students in early elementary will understand enjoyable and challenging physical activities, will develop self-confidence, and promote a positive self-image. Students begin to recognize their own abilities and choose activities/sports to improve their skills. By the end of 5th grade, students are able to better identify activities they enjoy and those in which they have greater skill or less skill. They articulate why they like or dislike certain activities. Although students can work cooperatively, they identify those classmates with whom they prefer playing or engaging in physical activity. Demonstrates passing and receiving with hands, feet, or implement with competency while moving, changing direction, and speed.
Demonstrates a lead pass with competency, while stationary, to a moving receiver.
Grade 7
Performs passing and receiving with hands, feet, or implement with competency while moving, changing direction and speed during small-sided game play.
Demonstrates a lead pass with competency, while moving, to a moving receiver.
Grade 8
Performs passing and receiving with hands, feet, or implement with competency while moving, changing direction, speed or level in small-sided game play.
Performs a lead pass with competency, while moving or stationary, to a moving receiver during small-sided game play.
Dribbling
Grade 6
Demonstrates dribbling skills with dominant hand, foot, or implement with control while moving, changing direction and speed.
Grade 7
Performs dribbling skills with dominant and nondominant hand, foot, and implement with control while moving, changing directions and speed in a variety of practice tasks.
Grade 8
Performs dribbling skills with dominant and nondominant hand, foot, and implement with control while moving, changing directions and speed in small-sided game play.
Striking
Grade 6
Demonstrates striking with competency in a closed environment.
Demonstrates striking a stationary object for accuracy, using an implement, with competency in activities (such as golf, hockey).
Demonstrates striking a moving object with competency using an implement with force in a variety of practices.
Grade 7
Performs striking with competency in a dynamic environment.
Performs striking a stationary object for accuracy and distance, using an implement, with competency in activities (such as golf, hockey).
Performs striking a moving object to open space, with competency, using an implement in a variety of practices.
Grade 8
Performs striking with competency in small-sided game play.
Performs striking a stationary object for accuracy and power, using an implement, with competency in activities (such as golf, hockey).
Performs striking a moving object for power, with competency, using an implement in small-sided game play.
Forehand and Backhand
Grade 6
Demonstrates forehand and backhand strokes with competency while transferring weight with correct timing.
Grade 7
Performs forehand and backhand strokes with competency while transferring weight with correct timing using a short or long handled implement in a dynamic environment.
Grade 8
Performs forehand and backhand strokes with competency while transferring weight with correct timing using a short or long handled implement during a small- sided game.
Shooting
Grade 6
Demonstrates shooting on goal with competency during a closed environment practice.
Grade 7
Performs shooting on goal with competency and accuracy during a dynamic environment.
Grade 8
Performs shooting on goal with competency and accuracy during a small-sided game.
Serving
Grade 6
Demonstrates an underhand or overhand serve with competency, control, and weight transfer.
Grade 7
Performs an underhand or overhand serve to a target with competency, control and weight transfer.
Grade 8
Performs an underhand or overhand serve with competency, control and weight transfer in a small-sided game.
Volleying
Grade 6
Demonstrates a controlled forehand volley with mature form with a short-handled implement.
Grade 7
Performs controlled forehand and backhand volleys with competency with a short or long handled implement in a dynamic environment.
Grade 8
Performs controlled forehand and backhand volleys with competency with a short or long handled implement during a small-sided game.
Offensive Skills
Grade 6
Demonstrates movement without the ball or object (such as pivot, give and go, and fakes).
Demonstrates movement with the ball or object (such as dribbling) without defensive pressure to create open space.
Grade 7
Performs at least one movement without the ball or object (such as the pivot, give and go, fakes, or jab steps).
Performs a least one movement with the ball or object (such as dribbling) against defensive pressure to create open space.
Grade 8
Performs two different movements without the ball or object (such as the pivot, give and go, fakes, or jab steps)
Performs two different movements with the ball or object (such as dribbling) to create open space during a small-sided game.
Defensive Skills
Grade 6
Demonstrates the ready position in defense by weight on balls of feet, arms extended, and eyes on the midsection of the offensive player.
Grade 7
Performs the defensive position and slides in all directions without crossing the feet in a dynamic environment.
Grade 8
Performs the defensive position and slides in all directions without crossing the feet in a small-sided game.

Standard 2: The physically literate individual applies knowledge of concepts, principles, strategies and tactics related to movement and performance.

Rationale: Middle grade students begin to learn and apply movement concepts (body awareness, spatial awareness, qualities of movement, and relationships) that enhance performance. They exhibit a higher level of complexity and breadth in learning movement skills, developing game strategies, and applying interdisciplinary knowledge (e.g. anatomy, physics) to game situations.
Individual Physical Activities
Target Games
Grade 6
Identifies the appropriate implement (such as a golf club, Frisbee) and/or shot based on location of the object in relation to the target.
Grade 7
Determines how to change speed and/or trajectory of the shot based on location of the object in relation to the target.
Grade 8
Demonstrates the concept of changing the speed, force, and trajectory of a shot based on location of the object in relation to the target.
Movement & Rhythm
Grade 6
Varies the application of force when performing movement activities.
Grade 7
Identifies Newton’s law of motion to various movement activities.
Grade 8
Describes Newton’s law of motion to various movement activities.
Outdoor Pursuits
Grade 6
Identifies appropriate decisions based on level of difficulty, due to conditions (weather) or ability, to ensure safety of self and/or others.
Grade 7
Analyzes the situation and makes appropriate decisions to ensure the safety of self and/or others.
Grade 8
Implements safety protocols in self-selected outdoor pursuits.
Games and Sport
Offensive Tactics
Grade 6

Demonstrates at least one way to create open space (such as moves to open space without a ball or object; uses a variety of passes, pivots, and fakes; give and go; uses the width and length of the field/court). (invasion games)
Identifies open spaces and attempts to strike object into the space. (field and strike games)
Grade 7

Demonstrates at least two ways to create open space (such as moves to open space without a ball or object; uses a variety of passes, pivots, and fakes; give and go; uses the width and length of the field/court; staying spread out on offense; cut and pass quickly). (invasion games)
Demonstrates a variety of shots to hit to open space. (field and strike games)
Grade 8

Applies multiple ways to create open space (such as moves to open space without a ball or object; uses a variety of passes, pivots, and fakes; give and go; uses the width and length of the field/court; staying spread out on offense; cut and pass quickly; uses fakes off the ball). (invasion games)
Performs a variety of shots to open space in a small-sided game. (field and strike games)
Defensive Tactics
Grade 6
Demonstrates at least one way to reduce open space (such as changing body position; by not allowing the catch (denial); allowing the catch, but not the return pass). (invasion games)
Identifies the correct defensive play based on the situation (such as number of outs). (field and strike games)
Grade 7

Demonstrates at least two ways to reduce open space (such as changing body position; by not allowing the catch (denial); allowing the catch, but not the return pass; staying close to the opponent as they near the goal). (invasion games)
Selects the correct defensive play based on the situation. (field and strike games)
Grade 8
Applies ways to reduce open space by staying on the goal side of the offensive player and anticipate the speed of the object or person for the purpose of interception or deflection.(invasion games)
Reduces open space during a small-sided game by working with teammates to maximize coverage. (field and strike games)
Transitions, Invasion Games
Grade 6
Demonstrates the transitions from offense to defense and defense to offense by recovering quickly.
Grade 7
Demonstrates the transitions from offense to defense and defense to offense by recovering quickly and communicating with teammates.
Grade 8
Demonstrates the transitions from offense to defense and defense to offense by recovering quickly, communicating with teammates and capitalizing on an advantage.
Creating Space, Net and Wall Games
Grade 6
Creates open space by varying force and direction.
Grade 7
Creates open space by varying force and direction, and forcing the opponent to move from side to side.
Grade 8
Demonstrates creating open space by varying force and direction, and forcing the opponent to move from side to side and/or forward and backward.
Tactics and Shots, Net and Wall Games
Grade 6
Demonstrates returning to the midcourt position to reduce options for offensive opponent.
Grade 7
Demonstrates an offensive shot based on opponent’s location (hit where opponent is not).
Grade 8
Demonstrates a variety of shots to end a rally by using placement, force, or timing.

Standard 3: The physically literate individual demonstrates the knowledge and skills to achieve and maintain a health-enhancing level of physical activity and fitness.

Rationale: Middle grade students begin to recognize the importance of physical activity and make independent decisions related to being active and maintaining a healthy quality of life. They seek out activities that will enhance their physical well-being in physical education class and during their free time. Moreover, they begin to make their own decisions and develop plans to enhance their own health- related physical fitness (muscular strength and endurance, flexibility, body composition, and cardiorespiratory endurance). They participate in moderate to vigorous physical activities that are linked to their physical skills and levels of fitness.
Physical Activity
Physical Activity Benefits
Grade 6
Describes how being physically active leads to a healthy body.
Grade 7
Identifies barriers related to maintaining a physically active lifestyle and identifies solutions for eliminating those barriers.
Grade 8
Explains connections between physical activity and overall physical and mental health.
Engagement in Physical Activity
Grade 6
Participates in self-selected physical activity outside of physical education class.
Grade 7
Participates in physical activity twice a week outside of physical education class.
Grade 8
Participates in physical activity three time a week outside of physical education class.
Fitness
Components of Fitness
Grade 6
Identifies the skill-related fitness components.
Grade 7
Identifies the difference between health-related and skill-related fitness.
Grade 8
Explains health-related and skill-related components of fitness for self-selected physical activities.
Health-Related Fitness
Grade 6
Differentiates between aerobic and anaerobic physical activity.
Demonstrates correct techniques and methods of stretching.
Uses pacing in cardiorespiratory endurance activities.
Grade 7
Differentiates between muscular strength and muscular endurance activities.
Describes and demonstrates the differences between dynamic and static stretches.

Describes the relationship between cardiorespiratory activities and exercise intensity (such as the Borg Rating of Perceived Exertion (RPE), the OMNI Scale, Heart Rate Monitors, or taking a heart rate manually).
Grade 8
Describes the impact of cardiorespiratory endurance, muscular endurance, and muscular strength on body composition.
Uses a variety of appropriate static and dynamic stretching techniques for different muscle groups.
Calculates target heart rate zone and adjust intensity during physical activity to stay in the zone.
FITT Principle
Grade 6
Describes each component of the FITT principle (frequency, intensity, time, type) for cardiorespiratory endurance.
Grade 7
Describes the FITT principle (frequency, intensity, time, type) for muscular endurance, muscular strength, and flexibility.
Grade 8
Designs a personal workout using the FITT principle (frequency, intensity, time, type).
Phases of Exercise
Grade 6
Describes the role of warm-ups and cool-downs before and after physical activity.
Grade 7
Designs a warm-up or cool-down for a self-selected physical activity.
Grade 8
Designs and implements a warm-up or cool-down for a self-selected physical activity.
Engagement in Fitness Activities
Grade 6
Participates in a variety of cardiorespiratory endurance activities.
Grade 7
Participates in a variety of cardiorespiratory endurance, muscular endurance, and muscular strength activities.
Grade 8
Participate in a variety of self-selected fitness activities outside of school.
Body Systems
Grade 6
Identifies major muscles used in selected physical activities.
Grade 7
Describes how muscles pull on bones to create movement in pairs by relaxing and contracting.
Grade 8
Explains how respiratory, muscular, and skeletal systems interact with each other during physical activity.
Nutrition
Grade 6
Compares and contrasts caloric expenditure for a variety of physical activities.
Grade 7
Explains the relationship of caloric intake and expenditure to weight management and investigates strategies for balancing calories.
Grade 8
Develops strategies for balancing healthy food, snacks, and water intake specific to daily physical activity.
Physical Activity and Fitness Planning
Goal-Setting
Grade 6
Uses a SMART (specific, measurable, attainable, realistic, and timely) goal to improve or maintain one area of health-related fitness based on a fitness assessment.
Grade 7
Uses a SMART (specific, measurable, attainable, realistic, and timely) goal to improve or maintain two areas of health-related fitness based on a fitness assessment.
Grade 8
Uses a SMART (specific, measurable, attainable, realistic, and timely) goal to improve or maintain three areas of health-related fitness based on a fitness assessment.
Physical Activity and Nutrition Log
Grade 6
Maintains and reflects on a personal physical activity log to document learning.
Grade 7
Maintains and reflects on a personal physical activity and hydration log to document learning, and set goals for improvement.
Grade 8
Maintains and reflects on a personal physical activity and nutrition log to document learning, and set goals for improvement.

Standard 4: The physically literate individual exhibits responsible personal and social behavior that respects self and others.

Rationale: Middle grade students use problem solving skills in choosing to participate in physical activities. They demonstrate an understanding of positive conduct in accordance with rules and policies. Middle grade students characterize differences in people based on skill level, physical status, social background, ethnicity, and gender as well as beginning to display empathy and appreciation for those in less fortunate situations while seeking out opportunities to help those in need.
Personal Responsibility
Grade 6
Exhibits personal responsibility by using appropriate etiquette, demonstrating respect for the facilities, and exhibiting safe behaviors.
Grade 7
Exhibits responsible social behaviors by cooperating with classmates, demonstrating inclusive behaviors, and supporting classmates.
Grade 8
Accepts responsibility for improving one’s own level of physical activity and fitness.
Rules and Etiquette
Grade 6
Identifies rules and etiquette for physical activities, games, dance and rhythmic activities.
Grade 7
Demonstrates knowledge of rules and etiquette by self-officiating physical activities and games or following parameters to create or modify a dance or rhythmic activity.
Grade 8
Applies rules and etiquette as an official for physical activities and games, and creating dance or rhythmic routines within a given set of parameters.
Receiving and Providing Feedback
Grade 6
Demonstrates responsibility by providing and accepting corrective feedback to improve performance.
Grade 7
Provides corrective feedback to a peer using teacher-generated rubric while using appropriate tone and other communication skills.
Grade 8
Provides encouragement and feedback to peers without prompting.
Working with Others
Grade 6
Cooperates with a small group of classmates during physical activities.
Grade 7
Demonstrates cooperation by establishing rules and guidelines for resolving conflicts.
Grade 8
Demonstrates cooperation skills and strategies that promote team or group dynamics.
Safety
Grade 6
Uses physical activity and fitness equipment appropriately and safely with teacher’s guidance.
Grade 7
Independently uses all equipment for physical activity and fitness appropriately and safely.
Grade 8
Identifies specific safety concerns associated with physical activity and fitness equipment.

Standard 5: The physically literate individual recognizes the value of physical activity for health, enjoyment, challenge, self-expression and/or social interaction.

Rationale: Middle grade students are emerging learners as it relates to their valuing the positive health and social outcomes that come from living a physically active lifestyle. They recognize their own likes, dislikes, strengths and skills, and use these to choose physical activities for enjoyment. Through a variety of activities students demonstrate an understanding of the importance of positive conduct and social interactions in accordance with rules and policies, and they build their ability to promote the respect for self and others.
Health
Grade 6
Describes how being physically active can lead to a healthy body.
Grade 7
Identifies different types of physical activities and describes how each has a positive impact on health.
Grade 8
Identifies the five components of health-related fitness and explains the connections of being healthy (physically and mentally) and fit.
Challenge
Grade 6
Applies strategies for overcoming individual challenges in a physical activity setting (such as extending effort, asking for help or feedback, or modifying the tasks).
Grade 7
Uses positive strategies when faced with a group challenge (such as offering suggestions or assistance, leading or following others, and providing possible solutions).
Grade 8
Applies strategies to overcome individual challenges in physical activity.
Self-Expression and Enjoyment
Grade 6
Describes how moving competently in a physical activity setting creates enjoyment.
Identifies how self-expression and physical activity are related.
Grade 7
Identifies why self-selected physical activities create enjoyment.
Explains the relationship between self-expression and lifelong enjoyment through physical activity.
Grade 8
Discusses how enjoyment can be increased in self-selected physical activities.
Identifies and participates in an enjoyable activity that prompts individual self-expression.
Social Interaction
Grade 6
Demonstrates respect for self and others by following the rules and encouraging others in various physical activities and games.
Grade 7
Demonstrates importance of social interaction by avoiding negative talk, helping and encouraging others in various physical activities and games.
Grade 8
Demonstrates respect for self and others by asking for help and helping others in various physical activities and games.
High School

Standard 1: The physically literate individual will demonstrate competency in a variety of motor skills and movement patterns.

Rationale: High school students typically attain proficiency of motor skills and movement patterns within units of instruction they are familiar with and strive toward proficiency in more novel units of instruction. The key element in facilitating a physically literate high school student is to afford them choice.
Lifetime Activities
Outdoor Pursuits, Individual, Partner/Team Sports
High School Level 1 (PE I & II, Required Courses)
Demonstrates competency in activity-specific movement skill in two or more lifetime activities such as outdoor pursuits, individual performance activities, aquatics, net/wall games or target games.
High School Level 2 (Elective PE)
Improves on activity-specific skill in one or more activities (such as biking, orienteering, badminton, tennis, soccer, volleyball, basketball, ultimate).
Dance and Rhythms
High School Level 1 (PE I & II, Required Courses)
Demonstrates competency in one or more of the following: jump rope, tinikling sticks (jump bands), Zumba, hip hop, modern, square, line, social or choreographing a dance routine).
High School Level 2 (Elective PE)
Improves on activity-specific skill in one or more genres such as: jump rope, tinikling (jump bands), Zumba, hip hop, line, modern, ballet, cultural, swing, or ballroom).
Fitness Activities
High School Level 1 (PE I & II, Required Courses)

Demonstrates competency in one or more specialized skills in health-related fitness activities (such as Yoga, Pilates, resistance training, running, fitness walking, Zumba, aquatics, circuit training).
High School Level 2 (Elective PE)
Improves on activity-specific skill in one or more activities (such as group exercise, circuit training, resistance training, Yoga, Pilates, martial arts, running, aquatics).

Standard 2:  The physically literate individual applies knowledge of concepts, principles, strategies and tactics related to movement and performance.

Rationale: High school students strive for improving their skill level in motor skills by applying learned concepts associated with movement and through analysis of their own skills. They bring together many disciplines such as physics and anatomy to gain a better understanding of how and why they move as they do. Students assume performance outcomes based on movement principles and plan their goals for improvement.
Movement concepts, principles and knowledge
Movement Performance
High School Level 1 (PE I & II, Required Courses)
Applies the terminology associated with exercise and participation in individual-performance activities (such as dance, net/wall games, target games and/or outdoor pursuits appropriately).
Uses movement concepts to analyze and improve performance of self and/or others in a selected skill.
Develops a practice plan to improve performance for a required or self-selected skill.
Demonstrates training principles and knowledge to a required or self-selected activity.
High School Level 2 (Elective PE)
Applies concepts associated with self-selected activities for improvement of knowledge and competency.
Uses principles associated with self-selected activities to develop a plan for improved performance.
Utilizes strategies and tactics of selected activities for successful participation.
Applies training principles and knowledge through a self-selected activity.

Standard 3: The physically literate individual demonstrates the knowledge and skills to achieve and maintain a health-enhancing level of physical activity and fitness.

Rationale:High school students participate regularly in a variety of physical activities of interest and availability that can be continued for a lifetime. These activities are representative of the goals and objectives previously designed into the student’s individual fitness program and are complementary to the student’s strengths and activity preferences. Furthermore, they utilize learned principles and current practices to assess their own fitness levels using a variety of assessment tools. They analyze the results of these assessments and design a fitness program that meets their needs and interests and builds upon previously acquired fitness skills.
Fitness
Health-Related Fitness
High School Level 1 (PE I & II, Required Courses)
Adjusts intensity to keep heart rate in the target zone, calculates recovery heart rate and applies both to a personal fitness plan.

Demonstrates muscular strength and muscular endurance exercises effectively (isometric, concentric, eccentric), such as using resistance bands, body weight, free weights, and resistance-training machines for personal fitness development.
Demonstrates flexibility exercises (static, dynamic, proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitation (PNF) for personal fitness development.
Designs and implements a fitness program, including all components of health-related fitness.
High School Level 2 (Elective PE)
Applies technology (such as wearable devices, mobile device apps, and/or social media tools) to support physical activity and lifetime fitness habits.

Displays basic competence and/or growth in each health-related fitness component and associated activities, such as:

Cardiovascular Fitness: fitness center equipment (such as treadmill, elliptical, bike ergometers, row machine, etc.) group aerobic exercise, circuit training, dance, running/walking, swimming, etc.

Muscle Fitness:
  1. Strength: Resistance training with free weights or selectorized machines, powerlifting/Olympic lifting, TRX, Kettlebell training, etc.
  2. Endurance: bodyweight training, calisthenics, Resistance bands, TRX, Yoga/Pilates, etc.
Flexibility:
  1. Active & Passive
    1. Dynamic, Static, and Ballistic stretching (individually or with a partner): common stretch and hold techniques, partner assisted stretches or activation stretches.
Body Composition
  1. Maintains a healthy caloric/energy balance for an active lifestyle.
Physical Activity
Physical Activity Knowledge
High School Level 1 (PE I & II, Required Courses)
Investigates the relationship between physical activity, nutrition, and body composition.
Evaluates risks and safety factors that might affect physical preferences throughout the lifespan.
Investigates activities that can be pursued in the local environment (such as health clubs, recreational leagues, indoor/outdoor trails, community centers).
Identifies issues associated with exercising in various types of weather conditions (such as heat, humidity, and cold).
High School Level 2 (Elective PE)
Identifies fitness principles (such as overload, recovery, specificity) and can apply them to a variety of physical activities in their personal fitness plan.
Lists opportunities to increase daily physical activity.
Describes community and school resources to engage in physical activity.
Engagement in Physical Activity
High School Level 1 (PE I & II, Required Courses)
Participates regularly in physical activity outside of the school day.
High School Level 2 (Elective PE)
Meets or exceeds the threshold of accumulating 60 minutes of daily moderate to vigorous physical activity (MVPA), including in and out-of-school time.
Physical Activity and Nutrition Planning
High School Level 1 (PE I & II, Required Courses)
Understands the relationship between caloric intake, physical activity and body composition.
High School Level 2 (Elective PE)
Adjusts daily nutritional intake to meet physical activity levels that work toward their own body composition goal.
Individual Plan
High School Level 1 (PE I & II, Required Courses)

Designs and implements a personal fitness and nutrition plan (assessment scores, goals for improvement, plan of activities for improvement, log of activities to reach goals, timeline for improvement.)
High School Level 2 (Elective PE)
Designs and uses a personal fitness plan that incorporates the health-related fitness components and follows the key principles of training.
Stress
Stress Management
High School Level 1 (PE I & II, Required Courses)
Identifies stress-management strategies such as mental imagery, relaxation techniques, deep breathing, aerobic exercise, meditation to reduce stress.
High School Level 2 (Elective PE)
Explains the positive health outcomes related to managing stress from engaging in regular physical activity and lifetime fitness pursuits.

Standard 4:  The physically literate individual exhibits responsible personal and social behavior that respects self and others.

Rationale: High school students recognize the influence of physical activity, exercise, and sport on society. They analyze the effects of cultural differences on the various types of physical activities, exercise, and sports seen in different parts of the world. Students explore the history and purpose of international competition and compare games and physical activities in different countries. They begin to develop their own feelings about inclusion of people with physical, cultural, and emotional differences in the physical activities in which they participate. Students analyze environments and situations for safety and apply this analysis to their physical activities to ensure maximum positive results with minimum safety hazards. They anticipate potential conflicts and strive to prevent them from happening or quickly resolve conflicts that do occur in socially acceptable ways.
Personal Responsibility
High School Level 1 (PE I & II, Required Courses)

Employs effective self-management skills to review time commitments (among individual student’s curricular/extracurricular agenda) to identify barriers and modify physical activity and exercise patterns accordingly.
High School Level 2 (Elective PE)

Takes responsibility for engaging in daily physical activity and regular participation in lifetime fitness pursuits (such as trying out new activities, giving full effort and attention to the opportunities before them, being a positive role model for others, etc.).
Rules and Etiquette
High School Level 1 (PE I & II, Required Courses)
Exhibits proper etiquette, respect for others and teamwork while engaging in physical activity.
High School Level 2 (Elective PE)
Adheres to established or developed rules for participation in physical activities, respects the etiquette aspects of participation, and displays a positive disposition.
Working With Others
High School Level 1 (PE I & II, Required Courses)
Solves problems and thinks critically when working with others during physical activity, both as an individual and in groups.
High School Level 2 (Elective PE)
Modifies the physical activity or lifetime pursuit so that all ability levels are meaningfully engaged.

Demonstrates the ability to engage in leadership roles in various physical activity settings to help facilitate successful participation (such as proposing rules/modifications, helping resolve conflicts, or deciding on an outcome).
Safety
High School Level 1 (PE I & II, Required Courses)

Both demonstrates and applies best practices for participating safely in physical activity and exercise (such as injury prevention, proper alignment, hydration, use of equipment, implementation of rules, sun protection).
High School Level 2 (Elective PE)
Differentiates an inherent risk versus an unsafe practice.

Standard 5:  The physically literate individual recognizes the value of physical activity for health, enjoyment, challenge, self expression and/or social interaction.

Rationale:  High school students recognize and respect that participating in physical activity can be accomplished in a lot of ways and for a lot of reasons. They can justify that each path to physical activity is unique and that it may change during various stages of life. A physically literate high school student values the various reasons for living a physically active life and can independently develop a plan for being active throughout their life.
Benefits
High School Level 1 (PE I & II, Required Courses)
Explains physical health benefits of attaining or exceeding the daily recommended 60 minutes of MVPA.
Identifies the relationship between engaging in physical activities and positive outcomes related to social interaction.
Identifies opportunities for social interaction in a self-selected physical activity.
High School Level 2 (Elective PE)
Analyzes physical health benefits of attaining or exceeding the daily recommended 60 minutes of MVPA.
Substantiates the relationship between engaging in regular physical activity and positive outcomes related to cognition and/or academic readiness.
Articulates positive social outcomes of trying a new physical activity with others.
Expression
High School Level 1 (PE I & II, Required Courses)
Participates in a self-selected physical activity for self-expression and enjoyment.
Chooses a new physical activity and/or choose an appropriate level of challenge to experience success.
High School Level 2 (Elective PE)
Shares the many ways that people of all ability levels and interests can accomplish 60 minutes of MVPA daily.
Highlights the personal growth aspects of engaging in a novel physical activity
